title: A green, versatile, and facile strategy for anti-biofouling surface with ultra-high graft density polyethylene glycol

predicted_errors.error_location: Preparation of PC-Cu@K6-PEG coating, pH adjustment description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: In the same Methods section, the text first says the PC solution pH 'was then adjusted to 5.5 with 0.1 M sodium hydroxide', but later states 'All the pH adjustments mentioned above were made using 1 mM salt. Specifically, 1 mM hydrochloric acid and 1 mM sodium hydroxide were used for the above pH adjustments.' These two stated concentrations for pH adjustment (0.1 M NaOH vs 1 mM HCl/NaOH) directly contradict each other.

The paper defines 'Hemolysis ratio (%) = (OD samples – OD negative) / (OD positive – OD negative)'. As written, this yields a dimensionless fraction from 0 to about 1, not a percentage. To express the result as a percentage, the formula must be multiplied by 100. The missing factor makes the stated 'Hemolysis ratio (%)' mathematically inconsistent with the formula.

predicted_errors.error_location: Rabbit catheter thrombus model / animal circulation description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that after 2 h of 'in vitro circulation' the catheters were removed and thrombus weight was measured. However, the described setup is a closed circulatory system created in living rabbits by cannulating the carotid artery and jugular vein. This is an in vivo/ex vivo perfusion model, not an in vitro circulation system. Calling it in vitro misdescribes the experimental setup.

The methods refer to 'E. coli and S. aureus epidermidis' as the two test organisms. 'S. aureus epidermidis' is not a valid bacterial species name; Staphylococcus aureus and Staphylococcus epidermidis are distinct species. The Materials section also lists only 'Escherichia coli (DH5α) and Staphylococcus aureus (SH1000)', so the later mention of 'S. aureus epidermidis' is biologically incorrect and inconsistent with the stated strains.

predicted_errors.error_location: Surface mechanical properties / adhesion energy description
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The text states that upon contact 'these attractive forces transform into repulsive forces, and the measured force corresponds to the adhesion energy of the coating.' Adhesion energy is a work-per-unit-area quantity, not a force; AFM pull-off measurements give an adhesion force, which can be converted to adhesion energy using a contact-mechanics model. Equating measured force directly with adhesion energy is physically incorrect.
